newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai political worries hit new bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Thai political worries hit new bond issues.

text.p: Political uncertainty, eroded foreign confidence and volatile Thai interest rates are delaying the launch of a growing list of new Thai corporate bonds.
Issues hit by delays include Securities One Plc's two billion baht ($80 million) senior debt, and IFCT Finance and Securities Plc's one billion baht bond.
Siam City Bank Plc treasury manager Enghug Nontikarn said he expected a delay for his bank's planned 4.5 billion baht bond issue.
Traders said Italian-Thai Development Plc's planned maximum five billion baht bond and Ch Karnchang Plc's 1.5-2.5 billion baht issue would be similarly affected.

Vipoota Trakulhoon, first executive vice-president of Phatra Thanakit Plc, expected a decision Wednesday on whether to put off the launch of phone service provider Total Access Communications Co's five billion baht bond previously scheduled for early October.
Dealers and issuers said debt market sentiment had been hurt by political troubles faced by outgoing Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa and volatility of Thai interest rates.
Banharn has announced he would resign by Friday in return for support from his five coalition partners to help win a no-confidence vote in parliament last Saturday.
Bangkok's depressed Bond Dealers Club saw its average daily trading turnover slump to 300 million baht this week from 1.5-2 billion two months ago.
Traders said blue-chip bond yields rose 70-100 basis points during the last three weeks.

Securities One's treasury head Sathapana Leoprapia said: "We're delaying it. I think the timing isn't good. We'll wait for the political situation to resolve, for the next government, and foreign confidence to return. We planned to bring it out in the first week of October but now it will probably be next year."
Foreign investors have bought up to 70 percent of Thai blue- chip debt papers.

A trader at Thai Investment and Securities Co Plc said: "Issuing firms have changed terms and coupons on a week by week basis to make their issues look good but after a while, funding costs become prohibitive and they realise it makes more sense to wait until the market improves."
